item.title: MetaMatch: Reconciling Metadata for Aggregating Music Difficulty Annotations
item.description:
Chris Willcocks, Megan Finch, Mark Gotham
The inconsistency of metadata across sources is a persistent problem for large-scale music research. The variety of approaches to documenting even basic elements such as artists’ names and work titles makes it difficult to aggregate data across different sources. This paper presents a comparative analysis of approaches to this problem, combining the OpenRefine Reconciliation pipeline with LLM-based strategies for entity matching. item.title: Step-labelled check reports for research papers: a proposal for Claude
item.description:
Abdukhomid Nurmatov
An author may check a paper with AI before submission, and a referee may check the same paper again; neither sees the other's results. I propose a Claude tool with which the author checks a paper once, step by step, and a Claude page that lists checked papers together with their reports. Every step of a report states whether and how it was checked, gives its justification, and has its own problem thread, so that referees can read the report instead of repeating the check.
